segments.title: 4. Video -> sprites, mocap and 3D
lines: Use YOUR OWN clips (one per move): walk, run, jump, punch ...
Video -> sprites cuts the person out of the footage and loops / times each move.
Video -> mocap drives the 3D mannequin with the tracked motion (GLB/FBX).
Orbit video -> 3D mesh is a guided photogrammetry route with console LODs.
The clips in this video are rendered test clips of the mannequin (no real people).

items: Clip 1: walking, camera on a tripod
Clip 2: running 'in frame' - the camera follows the runner, the background slides past

script.cap: Choose 'Video -> sprites': only the video fields are shown
One clip per move:  move:frames=file  ('Add clip...' picks the file for you)
Camera and background on 'auto': static / handheld / tracking and median / plate / green screen are detected
Optional console target: here SNES as well as the HD sprites
Cut-out, loop detection (one exact walk / run cycle), scaling to one ground line, SNES export
Done: the contact sheet shows the walk and run cycles cut out of the footage
Help > Video to sprites explains every step, filming tips and limits

items: Debug sheet for the tracking shot: frames, background panorama and the cut-out
All four test moves: walk, run, jump (handheld + empty plate), punch (green screen)
Video -> mocap: tracked body points (top) and the fitted mannequin (bottom)
The mocap moves in model.fbx, re-imported in Blender
Orbit video -> 3D mesh: CPU reconstruction and console LODs (PS2 5000 / PS1 600 tris)

segments.title: Limits (honest)
lines: Sprites are cut-outs of the real footage: hair, loose clothes, busy floors give rough edges.
Mocap: body only (no fingers / face); fast runs come out ~15-25 degrees less bent.
3D scan: the object must stay still; shiny / plain surfaces fail; not one-click.
For hero-quality textured models use Meshroom / RealityScan, then import the mesh here.
